name: Salmon calcitonin
lead: Salmon calcitonin is a synthetic form of calcitonin, a 32-amino-acid peptide hormone made by thyroid C cells that lowers blood calcium by inhibiting bone resorption. The salmon version differs from the human sequence at many positions and is reported to be more potent and longer acting [1][2].

The US prescribing label for calcitonin salmon injection lists indications for symptomatic Paget's disease of bone, hypercalcaemia, and postmenopausal osteoporosis when alternatives are unsuitable, noting that fracture-reduction efficacy has not been demonstrated for osteoporosis [2]. It is a bone-resorption inhibitor rather than a bone-building agent. The sources reviewed contain no documented looksmaxxing-community use or appearance-related studies.
infobox: Injection (subcutaneous, intramuscular); nasal spray formulations also exist
1962, Douglas Copp and colleagues, per Grokipedia

paras: The label describes calcitonin salmon as a calcitonin receptor agonist acting mainly on bone, with direct renal and gastrointestinal effects also recognised; calcitonin receptors are found on osteoclasts and osteoblasts, though the hormone's role in normal human bone physiology is described as not fully elucidated [2]. Grokipedia states it inhibits osteoclast function via G protein-coupled signalling [1].

Registered studies include a phase 3 trial of nasal salmon calcitonin on bone microstructure in postmenopausal women [3], a phase 4 trial of nasal calcitonin for muscle strength and pain after forearm fracture [4], and a terminated phase 3 trial of oral salmon calcitonin in knee osteoarthritis [5]. The label states that fracture-reduction efficacy has not been demonstrated for osteoporosis [2]. No studies of salmon calcitonin for height, facial structure or other appearance goals were found.

The label lists hypersensitivity reactions including reports of fatal anaphylaxis, hypocalcaemia, and malignancy, noting a meta-analysis of 21 clinical trials suggesting an increased risk of overall malignancies in calcitonin-treated patients; common adverse reactions are nausea with or without vomiting, injection-site inflammation and facial or hand flushing, and circulating antibodies may reduce response [2].

timeline.event: Calcitonin discovered by Douglas Copp and colleagues, according to Grokipedia [1].

card.summary: A fish-derived calcitonin used for Paget's disease and hypercalcaemia; it slows bone loss and has no documented appearance use.
card.note: Label warns of anaphylaxis, hypocalcaemia and a possible malignancy signal.

quick.overview:
Salmon calcitonin is a prescription peptide that slows bone breakdown. Doctors use it for Paget's disease of bone, high blood calcium and, when other drugs are unsuitable, postmenopausal osteoporosis.

No source reviewed shows looksmaxxing use or tests it for appearance.
quick.mechanism: It activates calcitonin receptors on bone-resorbing osteoclasts, reducing bone breakdown and calcium release.
quick.risks: The label lists anaphylaxis, low calcium, nausea, flushing and a possible increased malignancy risk. It is Rx-only.
